cards.text: After all those big promises from the LORD, you'd think King David would put his feet up for a while. NOPE. Some time later, David heads out to war, and friend, this chapter is one victory after another.

cards.question: Who does David defeat first, taking Metheg-ammah right out of their hand?

cards.text: Next, David defeats the Moabites. He makes them lie down on the ground and measures them off with a cord.

cards.question: Two lengths of David's cord marked the Moabites who would be put to death. One length marked the ones who would be ___.
Now the Moabites are subject to David. What do they start bringing him?

cards.text: Then comes Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah. He's marching out to restore his dominion along a big river, and David defeats him. Big plans, friend. Short trip.

cards.question: King Hadadezer had marched out to restore his dominion along the ___ River.

cards.text: David captures a thousand chariots from Hadadezer. SEVEN thousand charioteers. TWENTY thousand foot soldiers. Friend, I couldn't keep track of six cookie cutters on one counter.

cards.question: True or false: David keeps every one of Hadadezer's horses for his own chariots.

cards.text: Then the Arameans of Damascus come to help King Hadadezer of Zobah. Backup has ARRIVED.

cards.question: True or false: With the Arameans of Damascus helping, Hadadezer's side turns the battle against David.

cards.text: Not even close. David strikes down twenty-two thousand of their men. That's me diving to save a falling tray of cookies. Now there's a tray on the floor AND a stamper on the floor.

cards.question: David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans bring him tribute. Who does the chapter say made David victorious wherever he went?

cards.text: David takes the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's officers. From Betah and Berothai, Hadadezer's cities, he takes a large amount of bronze too. I came out of that drawer with ONE gold base, and I thought I was fancy.

cards.question: David brings the gold shields of Hadadezer's officers to ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Toi, king of Hamath, hears that David defeated Hadadezer's entire army. And Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. I bet Toi read that news twice just to enjoy it.

cards.question: King Toi sends someone to greet King David and bless him for defeating Hadadezer. Who does he send?
Joram brings King David articles of silver and gold and bronze. True or false: David keeps them for his own palace.

cards.text: David dedicates them to the LORD, along with the silver and gold from all the nations he subdued: Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Amalekites, plus Hadadezer's spoil. Me? Somebody hands me something shiny, it's going on the counter where EVERYBODY can see it.

cards.question: Back in 2 Samuel 7:9, the LORD told David, "Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land." Now David returns from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. What does he make for himself?

cards.text: There's that word again. Name. Then David places garrisons throughout Edom. Friend, this man is putting up garrisons like I put out cooling racks.

cards.question: True or false: Even with David's garrisons in Edom, some of the Edomites stay free of him.

cards.text: All the Edomites are subject to David. And that line again: "So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went." Now David reigns over all Israel.

cards.question: As he reigned over all Israel, David administered ___ and ___ for all his people.

cards.text: Then we meet David's team: Joab son of Zeruiah over the army, plus a recorder, priests, a scribe, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons are priestly leaders. That's a real org chart. Mine is me, me, and on busy days, also me.

findings.problem: The opening line 'After all those big promises from the LORD' states a fact from 2 Samuel 7, the context-only passage before this one. It gives no reference, and the card cites only 2 Samuel 8:1.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The answer is given away before the baker reaches the question. Card 1 says 'this chapter is one victory after another,' and card 6 already says David defeats Hadadezer. Both rule out 'True' before Hadadezer's backup arrives.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke compares capturing huge numbers of chariots and soldiers with not being able to keep track of six cookie cutters. Those aren't the same action, so the comparison doesn't click. The line also suggests he lost track of his kids, which clashes with the backstory, where he looked after them and caught them when they wobbled.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions the horses, so the true or false is pure luck. Answering 'False' also never tells the baker what actually happened: David hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots. That detail from 8:4 is missing from the walkthrough.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: 'Meanwhile' adds a time link the text doesn't give. Verse 9 says only 'When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer.'

rule.text: No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question quotes 2 Samuel 7:9, 'Now I will make for you a name...', just before asking what David makes for himself. The setup hands the baker the answer 'A name.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Several story cards after the opening card run longer than 2 sentences: stop 1 cards 6, 8, 12 and 14, and stop 2 cards 1, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Most have 3 or 4 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This two-blank card fixes 'justice' to blank 1 and 'righteousness' to blank 2. A baker who picks 'righteousness and justice' has the meaning right but the order swapped.
findings.question: On a two-blank fill in the blank, should a swapped order of the two right words count as right, or should cards avoid blanks where swapping keeps the meaning?
